implementation_state: Fully implemented and fixture-verified: auth, expiry/refresh, usage and quota, check-in, health. 57 unit tests run the adapter against an in-process fake panel, and 5 route-table tests fence endpoint provenance against upstream's Go source. The previous record said 'Not integrated: no production caller', and that statement is now false rather than merely dated: Desktop builds this adapter behind the opt-in account-maint feature, and checkin_commands::observe calls its check-in observation, so the adapter has a production caller that is reached whenever an operator starts a check-in. It stays PARTIAL for two reasons that replaced the old one. The integration has never been exercised against a real panel, so every claim here is still a claim about a fake. It was also unreachable in the default build, so no operator met it unless they went looking for it; that second reason is gone, because the shipped desktop app now carries the adapter. The one that remains is the first, and it is not a reason a code change can remove: no real panel has ever answered this adapter. Log-type interpretation is now transcribed from model/log.go at QuantumNous/new-api main instead of inferred from the constants, and the write sites there disagree with each other about what the quota column means — which is why a log row is never read as a balance delta. The record previously said usage/quota were unimplemented, which has not been true since before the node was re-examined. See E-114 and E-130.
unblock_condition: Pass a local mock-server auth/expiry/refresh/usage/quota contract before any real protocol E2E.
notes: No real NewAPI credential or provider call is evidence.
A production caller now exists and has still never touched a real panel. Reaching one in this repository's tests requires a credential nobody here has, so the gap is named rather than closed.

THE BALANCE IS NOW REACHABLE FROM THE PROVIDER ROW, WITH THE USER ACCESS TOKEN. The adapter was always able to read a panel's wallet — the reconciler has called it since the account work — but the balance it produced was visible only on the Accounts page, per account. A provider that declares no account had no balance at all, because every balance preset is relay-side and a NewAPI relay publishes none: it serves /v1 and keeps the wallet in the panel. The provider-level figure is now the sum of what its accounts report, read per provider and added only when they agree on the unit. A preset could not have supplied this: the panel answers to the account's credential, and a provider-level probe authenticates with the provider's relay key. So the gap was a shape, not a missing endpoint. The status stays PARTIAL and the two reasons it gives are unchanged by this: the integration has still never been exercised against a real panel, and the subsystem is still only reachable under an opt-in feature.

THE SHIPPED APP NOW CARRIES THE CAPABILITIES ITS OWN INTERFACE OFFERS. The desktop's default feature list was `["ml"]`, so the account subsystem, the NewAPI panel adapter, the browser check-in and the OpenCode provider kinds were all absent from the installed app — while the dashboard offered the account page, the check-in and both OpenCode kinds unconditionally. The panel said "this build contains no account subsystem" to the very people the product was written for, and the panel-backed balance was in the source tree and in no installation of it. **THE REASON THESE WERE KEPT OUT HAS EXPIRED, AND THE REASON IS WORTH KEEPING.** It was "the surface is not reachable yet: nothing probes an account, so with this on the store is constructed and stays empty". The reconciler landed, every declared account is probed and published, and that sentence no longer describes the code. **"OPTIONAL" NOW MEANS WHAT IT SHOULD MEAN: THE CAPABILITY IS IN THE BINARY AND THE BEHAVIOUR IS NOT.** Nothing probes an account until an account is declared; nothing asks a panel until an account exists and the button is pressed; no browser opens until the operator starts a check-in; the OpenCode providers only answer when one is configured. That is the shape ADR-0006 settled on for the learning stack, where `ml_routing.enabled` still defaults to off and an installation that has never promoted a model routes exactly as it did before. `--no-default-features` still builds a desktop app with none of it, so "ship without an account subsystem" remains a build rather than a deletion. The desktop's dependency line on `zroutery-core` still names no features at all, so the core's switches stay independently declared and the activation guard is untouched; `ml` is still first in the default list; and the core's own feature table is unchanged, so the learning build is not perturbed. See E-158.

THE SECOND OF THE TWO REASONS THIS NODE WAS PARTIAL IS NOW GONE, AND THE FIRST IS NOT. The node said it was partial because "it is reachable only under an opt-in feature, not in the default build, so no operator meets it unless they go looking for it". The shipped desktop app now carries the panel adapter, so an operator meets it by installing the app. What remains is the reason that cannot be removed by a code change: **no real panel has ever answered this adapter.** Every claim here is still a claim about a fake — 57 unit tests against an in-process panel and 5 route-table tests fenced against upstream's Go source are good evidence about the adapter's shape, and they are not evidence about a panel's behaviour. The node stays PARTIAL for that reason and no other, and it is now the *only* reason. See E-158.
